themes_detail.label: Illegal Animal Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Complaints about illegal animals kept as pets spiked to 3 THIS WEEK, a 700% increase versus the 0.4 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.42), signaling a possible emerging animal welfare or housing code enforcement issue in Flatlands/Canarsie.
evidence: 3 illegal animal complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Temporal clustering suggests concentrated incident or pattern, not random noise
reporting_angles: Interview animal control officers about what types of animals are being reported and why the spike is happening now
Investigate whether recent enforcement sweeps, landlord-tenant disputes, or housing code violations are driving complaints

themes_detail.label: Non-Emergency Police Calls Climb
themes_detail.summary: Non-emergency police matters complaints jumped to 7 THIS WEEK, an 81% increase from the 3.9 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 3.37), pointing to a potential uptick in quality-of-life incidents or resident perception of disorder.
evidence: 7 non-emergency police complaints THIS WEEK vs. 3.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Converges with unleashed dog and illegal animal spikes, suggesting broader public order concern
reporting_angles: Pull 311 complaint narratives to identify what specific non-emergency issues residents are calling about
Contact NYPD 70th Precinct to ask whether they've noticed patterns or resource constraints in responding to these calls

themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints skyrocketed to 11 complaints 2 WEEKS AGO, an 8700% spike from the 0.1 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 32.88, the highest severity signal in the dataset), indicating possible coordinated graffiti, unauthorized advertising, or political/commercial poster campaigns.
evidence: 11 illegal posting complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
8700% spike (z-score: 32.88, highest statistical anomaly in dataset)
Extreme z-score indicates this is not random variation; represents genuine shift in posting activity
reporting_angles: Visit the neighborhoods where complaints clustered 2 weeks ago to photograph and document what type of postings remain visible
Interview Department of Sanitation about removal response times and whether they detected a coordinated campaign

themes_detail.label: Unleashed Dog Reports Triple
themes_detail.summary: Unleashed dog complaints jumped to 3 LAST WEEK, a 1100% increase from the 0.2 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.35), suggesting a potential uptick in dog-walking violations or animal control enforcement gaps.
evidence: 3 unleashed dog complaints last week vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Aligns with illegal animal and non-emergency police spikes, suggesting broader quality-of-life enforcement issue
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Parks enforcement and animal control to determine whether staffing or patrol frequency changed recently
Speak with residents in high-complaint areas to understand whether there are specific dog owners or parks driving the problem

themes_detail.label: Street Obstruction Complaints Jump
themes_detail.summary: Obstruction complaints rose to 25 LAST WEEK, a 115% increase from the 11.6 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.59), likely reflecting illegal parking, sidewalk encroachments, or vendor placement issues in public space.
evidence: 25 obstruction complaints last week vs. 11.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Complements ongoing high volume of illegal parking (2735 over 90 days) and blocked driveways (1922), indicating chronic street management problem
reporting_angles: Analyze 311 complaint text to distinguish between illegal parking obstructions, construction encroachments, and vendor sidewalk use
Interview community leaders about whether recent infrastructure work, special events, or policy changes triggered the spike
